About the role
 The Data Analyst Assistant role is central to our current engagement with a Dubai-based investment firm that requires precise data handling and clear visualization. This position provides the quantitative groundwork that allows our principals to form a view on complex corporate governance and strategy questions. We need an assistant who can organize messy data sets into logical structures that reveal the health and performance of a holding company.

About Arabian Private Holdings
 Arabian Private Holdings was founded on the principle that many critical business problems do not fit the traditional large-firm consulting model. A board facing a succession question or a family group weighing a capital injection does not need a team of twelve associates and a hundred-page methodology deck. They need experienced partners who can sit with a problem, form a rigorous view, and defend it. We take on a limited number of mandates to ensure that every client receives direct attention from the principals who are actually accountable for the outcome. Our work covers corporate strategy, governance, and operating model efficiency for some of the most significant family groups, listed corporations, and government entities in the region. We focus on clarity over complexity. We operate as a remote firm, choosing to prioritize the quality of our analysis and the strength of our relationships over traditional office overhead or aggressive growth targets.

What you will do
  • Collect and organize financial and operational data from various portfolio companies for a Dubai-based investment.
  • Clean and validate data sets to ensure accuracy before they are used in client presentations.
  • Build simple, effective spreadsheets that track performance indicators for large holding companies.
  • Assist in drafting reports that translate numbers into clear written arguments for our principals.
  • Monitor industry trends and perform basic market research to support ongoing strategic mandates.
  • Maintain internal records to ensure that historical client data is easily accessible and correctly categorized.
  • Prepare charts and graphs that simplify complex financial structures for board-level reviews.
  • Support the audit of corporate governance documents by cross-referencing quantitative findings with qualitative reports.


What we are looking for
  • A clear understanding of basic statistics and a logical approach to problem-solving.
  • Proficiency in spreadsheet software with an ability to manage large amounts of information without errors.
  • Strong written skills and the ability to explain what a set of numbers means in plain English.
  • Curiosity about how large corporations and family groups operate in different sectors.
  • Precision in your work, where you check your own calculations before submitting them for review.
  • A degree or ongoing studies in a quantitative field such as economics, finance, or mathematics.


How we work
 We operate as a fully remote firm, which means we rely on clear documentation and asynchronous communication. Because our work involves sensitive mandates for high-profile clients, we maintain a high standard of professional conduct and data security. You will work closely with a principal who provides direct mentorship and expects you to form your own view on the data you analyze. We do not value long hours for the sake of appearances. Instead, we focus on the rigor of the output and the clarity of the logic. This remote model allows us to hire individuals based on their intellectual capability rather than their physical location, ensuring we can provide the best possible advice to our clients.

What the role offers
  • A paid entry-level position with a competitive compensation package for the current market.
  • Direct exposure to high-level corporate strategy and governance mandates.
  • Mentorship from experienced principals who have managed some of the largest holding companies in the region.
  • The flexibility of a permanent, full-time role that is entirely remote.
  • Practical experience in forming a rigorous view on business performance and portfolio health.

About Abacum

Abacum is the leading Business Planning solution for finance teams to drive performance. By automating reporting, enabling collaboration, and simplifying planning and forecasting, we help finance teams shift from number crunching to driving strategic decisions.

Founded in 2020 by two former CFOs, we’ve grown into a global team of 100+ people across 30+ nationalities. Headquartered in New York, we have offices in Toronto and Barcelona. We’re trusted by industry leaders such as Dish Networks, Strava, BetterUp, Kajabi, JG Wentworth, Abridge, Cortex, and hundreds more.

We have raised over $100m, closing in June 2025 our $60M Series B, led by Scale Venture Partners, with the strong participation of Cathay Innovation, Y Combinator, Atomico, Creandum, and angel operators from Adyen, Zapier, and Twitch.

Our mission is ambitious and we can’t do it alone - join Abacum as we build the future of Business Planning!

We are looking for...

An enterprise seller who already knows the Office of the CFO. You've carried a number selling planning, EPM, FP&A or finance software. You know how a CFO buys, how a steering committee stalls, and how to get a multi-stakeholder deal signed.

At Abacum you'll own a named territory of enterprise and upper mid-market accounts across EMEA. Many of them run legacy planning tools or spreadsheets that can't keep up with the business. Your job is to show them a better foundation, and win.

As an Enterprise Account Executive, you will...

- Own the full sales cycle for a named book of enterprise accounts, from first meeting to signed contract

- Build and run your own pipeline through targeted outbound, events, and partner co-selling with ERP vendors and implementation partners

- Sell to CFOs, VPs of Finance and Heads of FP&A, and bring IT, procurement, security and legal along the way

- Run complex evaluations: discovery, business cases, proofs of concept, and competitive displacements

- Forecast with discipline and keep a clean pipeline in CRM

- Work with Solutions Engineering, Product and Leadership to shape deals, and feed what you hear in the market back into the roadmap

What we need...

- 6+ years of quota-carrying B2B SaaS sales, with at least 3 years closing enterprise deals

- Experience selling EPM, FP&A, planning, or other Office-of-the-CFO software (finance, ERP, spend, or data platforms)

- A track record of closing six-figure ARR deals with 3–6 month cycles and hitting or beating quota

- Comfort leading multi-stakeholder deals with finance, IT, procurement and security at the table

- Experience displacing an incumbent, whether a legacy system or a spreadsheet-based process

- A consultative, value-based approach: you build a business case in a CFO's language

- The drive to build your own pipeline, not wait for inbound

- Clear, sharp written and verbal communication, including running demos with senior buyers

- Based in EMEA, with the ability to travel to customers and events

Bonus points if you have...

- Sold with or through ERP ecosystems (NetSuite, Sage Intacct, Microsoft Dynamics) or implementation partners

- Worked in finance, or you're comfortable talking models, drivers and variances with an FP&A team

- Used a structured sales method (MEDDPICC, Command of the Message, or similar)

- Been an early seller at a scaling company and helped build the enterprise playbook

Why sell Abacum

You know the category. Here's why this is the product you want in your bag.

1. A market ready to switch. Finance teams are stuck between rigid legacy planning tools that need a rebuild every time the business changes, and spreadsheets and AI tools no one can trust. Abacum is the governed, AI-native foundation that fixes both. That's a displacement story you can tell in every account.

2. AI that stands up to a CFO. Plenty of vendors claim AI. Ours runs on a governed financial model, so the AI reasons and the math stays exact. CFOs and IT teams can trust the output, and that wins technical evaluations.

3. Faster time to value than legacy EPM. 700+ integrations and self-service data pipelines mean customers see value in weeks, not after a long implementation. That shortens your cycle and makes the business case easy to sign.

4. Channels that bring you deals. Abacum is the only FP&A platform to pass NetSuite's SuiteCloud Developer Network review, is listed on the Sage Intacct Marketplace, and is a verified Microsoft Dynamics 365 partner. Those ecosystems and our implementation partners mean co-sell pipeline, not just cold outbound.

5. A product that keeps getting stronger. New AI skills ship every week. Abacum works where finance already works: Excel, Slack, Claude and ChatGPT, through MCP-native infrastructure. You'll have something new to show every quarter.

6. Funded to win enterprise. Abacum raised a $60M Series B to scale into larger customers. You'll join as we build the enterprise motion, with the room to shape it and grow with it.

What you get

- Competitive base, uncapped commission, and equity

- Remote in EMEA, with hubs in New York, Toronto and Barcelona

- Direct access to leadership and a real say in how we sell to enterprise

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation including equity package

  • Competitive vacation policy

  • Medical Insurance

  • L&D budget

  • Access to Meditopia (wellbeing platform)

  • Language courses (English / Spanish)

Our Values

Customer Obsession: We share the understanding that Abacum's sole purpose is to create value for customers and relentlessly deploy all creativity and energy to that end.

Audacious Ambition: We dream big and embrace discomfort. We assume risks, make on-time mistakes and learn how to methodically accomplish our goals.

Good People: We are self-reflective and praise diversity of thought. We don't justify the end with the means and know where to draw the line. We have fun every day.

Tough Love: We truly care for everyone in the team and embrace honest feedback and radical candor as ways to genuinely help each other.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status.

jobs.title: Senior Analyst, Permanent Control
jobs.description:
Company Description

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.


Please make your application, including your CV, in English Language. We are a global compliance team headquartered out of London.

About the role

As a Senior Analyst – Permanent Controls, you will join the Permanent Controls team, a global Second Line of Defence (2LoD) function based across Paris and Mauritius. Reporting directly to the Head of Permanent Controls within the Compliance department, you will focus on the financial perimeter, exercising second-line control, independent oversight, and framework monitoring over the organization's finance domain. You will partner closely with the First Line of Defence (1LoD) to establish control standards, design control matrices, and provide guidance when needed. You will also execute 2LoD control plans, issue formal findings, and track recommendations through to resolution.

 

Sitting in the Second Line of Defense, the global Permanent Controls team serves as an ongoing, trusted advisor and objective challenge to operational teams (1LoD), helping them design robust controls and ensure operational integrity across the organization.

Unlike periodic audit functions, Permanent Controls operates continuously to proactively identify vulnerabilities, standardize control frameworks, and foster a strong risk culture.

 

Note on Governance: This is a 2LoD function focused on ongoing control design, execution, and 1LoD enablement. It is distinct and independent from the Internal Audit (3LoD) function within Checkout.com.

 

Key responsibilities

  • Control Design: Collaborate with stakeholders to translate identified risks into comprehensive 2nd line control plans, standards, and templates.

  • 1LoD Enablement: Partner with the First Line of Defence teams to design, refine, and assess their control matrices, ensuring alignment with internal standards and regulators' expectations (ACPR, FCA..).

  • Execution & Testing: Formalize and execute second line permanent controls across critical perimeters, including:

    • Financial regulatory reporting across global entities (France, UK, US, etc.).

    • Accuracy of financial data, accounting standards, and reconciliations.

    • Internal financial processes, procedures, and statutory compliance (including the Order of 3 December 2014).

    • Safeguarding mechanisms (flow of funds, compliance with safeguarding measures, timelines, and incident monitoring).

  • Reporting & Escalation: Present detailed control findings and anomaly reports to the Head of Permanent Controls; track the implementation of remediation recommendations.

  • Proactive Continuous Improvement: Identify operational control gaps, take the initiative to propose practical solutions, and drive improvements to the overall control framework.

  • Tooling & Automation: Contribute to the implementation and optimization of automated control tools, tracking dashboards, and recommendation monitoring systems whenever possible.

 

About You

  • Experience: 5 years of experience in Financial Audit, Internal Control, or Financial Reporting within the financial services (banking, Fintech..) or payments industry.

  • Regulatory Context: Familiarity with regulatory frameworks and ACPR expectations is strongly preferred.

  • Mindset & Working Style:

    • Proactive & Autonomous: A "go-getter" who takes ownership, anticipates control gaps, and brings actionable solutions to the table rather than waiting for direction.

    • Naturally Curious: A drive to understand end-to-end business operations, data flows, and complex payment mechanics.

    • Rigorous & Analytical: Meticulous attention to detail with an ability to leverage data analytics to evaluate controls, transactions and processes objectively.

  • Languages: Fluency in French and English is required.

  • Communication: Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to communicate clear findings and influence decision-making across lines of defence.

 

Additional Information

Bring all of you to work

We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.

Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands.

We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here.

It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable.

Life at Checkout.com

We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection.

Curious about what it’s like to be part of our team? Visit our Careers Page to learn more about our culture, open roles, and what drives us.

For a closer look at daily life at Checkout.com, follow us on LinkedIn and Instagram

I joined hx in January 2025 as a Senior People Partner and have recently stepped into the People Lead role. Outside of work, I’m an F1 fan and dog mum, so I’m no stranger to fast-paced environments or the occasional pit stop for walkies.

Our People team supports all things people at hx, from performance and engagement to the systems, insights and day-to-day operations that help our teams do their best work.

We’re growing the team and looking for someone to own our People reporting and analytics, while helping keep the operational side of the function running smoothly.

It’s a great opportunity for someone who enjoys turning data into meaningful insights, wants to make a real impact and is excited to help shape how the People team grows alongside the business.

Interested? Read more about the role and life at hx below.

About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision, helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally, already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do, from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure, it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure. If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the People team

Our People team owns the systems and data that keep hx a high-performance, high-engagement place to work: performance and growth, people analytics, compensation and benefits, and HR compliance. We are building the reporting layer that lets the business make faster, better-evidenced decisions about its people rather than relying on instinct, and we work closely with Talent to connect hiring and pipeline data with performance and engagement data so leaders see the full employee lifecycle instead of fragments of it.

Inside People and Talent, AI has already changed how we screen, how we write up interviews and how we surface insight to leaders. There is far more to do. Plenty of what we do still runs on manual effort that could be designed out, and this role exists to go after that. We care much more about what you have built and put in front of real users than about the size of the team you have sat in, and impact here isn't tied to title or tenure.

You will work directly with People Leaders, with real scope to shape how the team works as we grow. One thing worth being direct about: there is no finished playbook here. If you need a well-defined remit and clear instruction to do your best work, this will be frustrating. If you would rather find the problem yourself and build the fix, you will have a lot of room..

What you'll be doing

  • Build the AI tooling that our People and Talent function runs on. Agents that answer the questions currently landing in our inbox, skills that draft the documents we write manually, workflows that pull our systems together. This is the core of the role rather than a project on the side.

  • Build out the People reporting layer, including dashboards on retention, attrition and engagement, and get to the point where you can tell us what the numbers mean, not just what they are.

  • Work with Talent to connect hiring and pipeline data to People data, and make that view something leaders can interrogate themselves.

  • Learn our people processes properly, starting with onboarding, payroll data integrity and the performance cycle, then rebuild the parts that depend on manual effort.

  • Support our performance review cycles in Lattice and our engagement surveys, help analyse what comes out of them, and automate the parts that should not need a person.

  • Help keep our HRIS data accurate, including records, reporting and system troubleshooting.

What you'll need to have done

  • Built and shipped something with AI that other people used, whether that is an agent, a script, a tool, a bot or a side project.

  • Got past the first version. We will ask how you tested it, what it got wrong with real users and what you changed as a result. If you have a long list of things you have experimented with, we want to hear what each one taught you.

  • Worked with more than one model or platform, and formed a view on what each is good for.

  • Worked with a real dataset, cleaned it up, and drawn a conclusion you could defend.

Bumble Inc. is the parent company of Bumble Date, BFF, and Badoo. The Bumble platform enables people to build healthy and equitable relationships, through Kind Connections. jobs.title: Forward Deployed AI Engineer
jobs.description:
gravity9 is a boutique IT consulting company headquartered in the UK with offices in the US, Canada, Poland, and Colombia. Our team has deep experience in engineering, experience design and product management. We enjoy a challenge and pride ourselves on working with our clients on their most complex problems, finding elegant and flexible solutions that help them transform their businesses.

Join Our Growing Team - Future Opportunities Await!

We are excited to share that our company is experiencing significant growth and expansion, and as a result, we're on the lookout for talented individuals to join our team.

We want to be upfront about our hiring process. At this moment, we are in the process of securing projects that align with our business goals and objectives. Our intention is to ensure that once we bring new team members on board, they will have a meaningful and impactful role to play from day one. While we might not be able to extend an offer immediately, we are highly interested in considering you for these future projects.

If you're open to the idea of potentially joining our team in the future, we encourage you to continue with our interview process. We value your time and effort and believe that getting to know you better will help us make an informed decision.

Once you have effectively concluded the entire recruitment procedure, we will retain your profile and reach out to you once a suitable opportunity emerges. Additional interviews will not be necessary at this stage, and we anticipate being able to extend an offer to you promptly.

What does the recruitment process look like?

1. Recruiter Screen

In the first call, our recruiter will learn more about you and your story to check a potential fit for gravity9. This is also an opportunity to ask your questions about the role and company. This step might take around 60 mins.

2. Tech 1 Interview with our AI Practice Lead

In this meeting your potential future teammate will take a deeper dive into your experience and what you could bring to the team.
This step will take around 75 mins.

3. Tech 2 Interview with our software consultants

In this meeting your potential future teammate will take a deeper dive into your experience and what you could bring to the team.
This step will take around 60 mins.

4. Final Interview

You made it to the very last stage! Here we already strive to cooperate with you and give you an opportunity to meet our leadership team during this informal talk. This step will take around 30 mins.

Thank you for considering the opportunity to be a part of our growing journey. We look forward to the possibility of working together and achieving great things.

Role Description

gravity9 is expanding its Forward Deployed Engineering team to build production agentic AI systems for enterprise clients, in partnership with leading frontier-model providers. We already support clients from different verticals to have agentic and RAG systems live in production across healthcare, financial services, retail and global logistics.

As a Forward Deployed AI Engineer you work embedded in the client's environment, from discovery, through architecture and build, to production and handover. This is end-to-end agent engineering, not proofs of concept and not advisory work. Two flavours of engagement:

  • Internal enterprise use cases, such as reconciliation and KYC workflows in financial services, clinical and claims workflows in healthcare, operations and supply-chain workflows in logistics.

  • Product- and customer-facing agents, more greenfield, often exploratory, built into the client's own product.

Engagements are typically a team of engineers over a few months, working shoulder-to-shoulder with the client's team including architects, DevOps and QA.

  • Embed with the client. Work hand-in-hand inside the client's environment, codebase and cloud tenancy, often in a hybrid team alongside their engineers. You are visible to the client from day one.

  • Design and build production agentic AI systems. Multi-agent orchestration, tool and function calling, retrieval, planning and routing, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, state and checkpointing, guardrails, failure handling and recovery.

  • Do the unglamorous data work. A large share of every engagement is data engineering: ingestion, flattening deeply nested structures, extracting content from unstructured documents, classification, summarisation, tagging, enrichment, indexing. Models reason over data, bad data beats a good model every time.

  • Own evaluation and accuracy. Establish a baseline eval dataset at the start of the engagement, automate grading, and track groundedness, faithfulness and retrieval quality per tool, not just at the agent level. Be ready to defend accuracy numbers to a sceptical enterprise stakeholder.

  • Engineer for cost and latency. Model selection and routing (cheaper, faster models for non-reasoning steps; frontier models where reasoning genuinely earns it), prompt and context budgeting, caching. Cost is a non-negotiable metric on every engagement.

  • Ship it properly. Observability and tracing, CI/CD, IaC, monitoring the client can actually operate, security and compliance review.

  • Transfer knowledge deliberately. We don't run a long-term support business. Every engagement is designed so the client owns and can extend the system after we leave. You architect with their team in the room, pair with their engineers, and hand over working monitoring and documentation.


Technical skills

Essential

  • Programming: Strong Python (async, typing, testing, packaging). Working competence in TypeScript / Node is a plus.

  • LLM application engineering: Hands-on production experience with frontier models: prompt and context engineering, structured outputs, tool and function calling, streaming, token and context-window management.

  • Agentic architecture: Built and shipped multi-agent or agentic workflows, planner/router patterns, supervisor and sub-agent designs, ReAct-style loops, state and checkpointing, retries and interrupts, human-in-the-loop review gates.

  • Frameworks: At least one of: Anthropic Agent SDK, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, or an equivalent orchestration framework, plus the judgement to know when to use none of them.

  • RAG and retrieval: Chunking strategy, embeddings, hybrid and semantic search, re-ranking, citation and provenance, natural-language-to-query translation.

  • Data platforms: NoSQL databases such as MongoDB (aggregation pipelines, Atlas Search, Atlas Vector Search) or a strong equivalent, plus SQL. Comfortable designing schemas for agent retrieval, not just for OLTP.

  • Data engineering: Building ingestion and enrichment pipelines over messy structured and unstructured sources, documents, PDFs, object storage.

  • Evaluation: Building eval harnesses and eval datasets, LLM-as-judge with its limits understood, regression testing of prompts and agents, metric selection per use case.

  • Cloud: Production delivery on AWS (incl. Bedrock), Azure or GCP, containers, serverless, networking basics, secrets management, IAM.

  • Engineering discipline: Git, code review, testing, CI/CD, IaC (Terraform or equivalent), observability.

Strong advantage

  • Anthropic certification (Claude Developer / Anthropic-issued credential), an explicit advantage at shortlisting.

  • Anthropic Agent SDK production experience, a significant bonus.

  • MCP (Model Context Protocol): building servers and clients, tool exposure, auth patterns.

  • Claude Code as an autonomous SDLC agent: sub-agents, hooks, custom skills, agent marketplaces, context sharing across a team.

  • LLM observability and tracing tooling (LangFuse, LangSmith, Arize, Braintrust or similar).

  • Regulated-environment delivery: HIPAA, GDPR, SOC 2, FCA/PRA, PII handling, data residency, guardrails and red-teaming.

  • Graph or taxonomy-based knowledge representation alongside vector retrieval.

  • Kafka / streaming, Databricks, or comparable large-scale data platform experience.

Nice to have

  • Voice and multimodal agents; evaluation of non-text outputs.

  • FinOps for AI workloads; unit-economics modelling for agent systems.

  • Open-source contribution to the agent / LLM ecosystem, or conference speaking.

  • Prior experience as an FDE, solutions architect, or delivery consultant at a frontier-model, data platform, or infrastructure vendor.

Soft skills

An FDE is an engineer who is safe in front of a client. We screen as hard on this section as on the technical one.

  • Client presence and credibility. Can hold a technical conversation with a client architect and a business conversation with their CTO or head of operations in the same hour, and be trusted by both. Can present, whiteboard, and answer hard questions without deflecting.

  • Translation. Turns a business problem described by non-technical people such as a clinician, campaign manager or supply-chain planner into a technical design, and explains the technical design back in their language.

  • Ego-free collaboration in a supporting role. On some engagements the tech lead will come from the client or a partner, not from us. You need to contribute strongly, disagree well, and take direction without friction. Brilliant-but-territorial doesn't work here.

  • Comfort with ambiguity and greenfield. Engagements often start before the requirements, the data access, or sometimes the problem statement are settled. You make progress anyway, and you make the ambiguity visible rather than hiding it.

  • Bias to production. Instinctively asks "how does this get deployed, monitored and maintained?" rather than stopping at a working notebook.

  • Teaching instinct. Actively enjoys upskilling the client's engineers, because self-sufficiency at handover is the definition of success, not follow-on billing.

  • Ownership and pace. Short engagements, small teams, no layers to hide behind. You unblock yourself, chase the access request, and follow the thread to the answer.

  • Commercial awareness. Understands that scope, cost and the client's willingness to pay are part of the engineering problem, and contributes to scoping and estimating honestly.

  • Resilience and adaptability. New client, new domain, new stack every few months; occasional travel; occasionally a sceptical stakeholder who has been told AI is coming for their job. You stay steady and constructive.

  • Written communication. Clear design docs, decision records, handover material and status updates in English. Much of this is asynchronous and cross-timezone.

  • Genuine curiosity about the field. This ecosystem changes monthly. We want people who are already reading, building side projects and forming opinions — not waiting for training to be scheduled for them.

Experience profile

  • FDE (mid): 3+ years software engineering, 1+ years hands-on LLM / agentic work with at least one system live in production. Client-facing exposure.

  • Senior FDE: 5+ years engineering, 2+ years AI or agentic AI, has owned the architecture of at least one production agent system end-to-end and led a client conversation about it.

  • Lead FDE: 7+ years, has led delivery teams of 3–7 people, can act as engagement tech lead, contributes to pre-sales and estimation, and can mentor a growing FDE bench.

What success looks like

  • First 90 days — owning a meaningful component of a client-facing agent system, including its evals, and trusted in front of the client.

  • 6 months — designing agent architectures independently, leading a workstream, and running the handover and knowledge-transfer track.

  • 12 months — a reference point for others on the team, contributing to reusable assets, pre-sales and interviewing.

What we offer

  • Support for vendor certifications and access to partner training programmes.

  • Company-wide AI tooling as part of how we work day to day.

It’s official: Bazaarvoice is a Great Place to Work in the US , Australia, India, Lithuania, France, Germany and the UK!

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is self-motivated, extremely curious, a strong communicator, patient, and highly enthusiastic about driving cross-team collaboration to meet our growth objectives.

jobs.title: Senior UI Designer
jobs.description:
Your mission

Native designs products that get made. Since 1997 we've worked across the US, Europe and Asia for the companies that take the object seriously: Bowers & Wilkins, Bang & Olufsen, Audi, Coloplast, Baxter, Bentley, HP and others we can't name yet. Along the way we've collected more international design awards than any independent studio in Europe. We've turned down every offer to be acquired because independence is what lets us tell a client the truth.
 
We're looking for a passionate, collaborative and creative Senior UI Designer with an impeccable eye for beauty, a head full of ideas and a strong sense of creative direction to join our studio in Shoreditch. We're hired to create wholly new products and experiences, so we're as much inventors as designers.
 
As a Senior UI Designer, you'll help define the future of our digital output, shaping remarkable experiences across tech, healthcare, wellness and automotive. You'll set visual design direction and deliver excellence across many platforms - from multi-modal AI experiences, beautiful UI, emotionally engaging motion design and 3D prototypes. You'll take ownership of creative output, grow into a mentorship role, and have a genuine influence on how the studio evolves.
 
You'll work with some of the world's best designers, developers, anthropologists, strategists, and engineers to make work that pushes boundaries, challenges perceptions, and - occasionally - changes the world.


Your profile

You
Here’s an idea of the sort of Senior UI Designer we hope is reading this: 

  • Experienced & Agency-Tested: You’ve honed your skills in a fast-paced, creative, (product, advertising, marketing or branding) agency environment, where you’ve delivered high-impact work across a range of industries.
  • Storyteller: You don’t just design, you shape narratives. You can articulate the thinking behind your work in a way that resonates with clients, teams, and users alike.
  • AI proficient: You actively explore new AI tools and thoughtfully integrate them into your workflow - not for novelty, but to elevate speed, craft, and thinking.
  • Cross-Disciplinary Fluent: You understand 3D and motion – bridging the gap between tactile and digital.
  • Visionary Thinker: You are full of ideas and bring creative thinking and technological curiosity to every challenge. You push what’s possible and influence others to do the same.
  • Leadership Minded: You're ready to step into a bigger role. You naturally guide more junior designers, earn trust across disciplines, and think about the craft at a studio level not just project level.
  • Craft-Led: You're obsessive about typography, hierarchy, layout, and interaction, with an eye for flawless visual execution.
  • Adaptable: We're not afraid to scrap an idea. Sometimes, we build it, test it, and start again. If this doesn't fill you with dread, and you're excited by the idea of being the person who helps shape what comes next, you'll make the work of your life at Native
  • Passionate: A passion for what you do is essential. We believe the best creatives genuinely enjoy their work.


Why us?

Us
Here's what you can expect from us:

  • Annual Leave 25 days’ holiday plus bank holidays. We actively encourage you to take your leave.
  • Enhanced Parental Leave Enhanced maternity and paternity pay.
  • Private Healthcare Bupa private medical insurance, including 24/7 GP access, mental health support, and specialist care. A health and wellness cashback plan.
  • Wellbeing & Fitness 40% discount across the Hussle Gym network. Access to YuLife wellbeing and fitness benefits, including mindfulness resources, company-wide challenges and cash rewards.
  • Professional Development Opportunities for learning and development, access to industry talks, exhibitions, and visiting speakers.
  • Studio Culture Regular company events and studio activities throughout the year.
  • Location Our Shoreditch studio is well connected and surrounded by a vibrant design and technology community.
  • Independent Studio Native has operated independently in East London for almost 30 years. We are committed to long-term thinking, craft, and delivering thoughtful innovation without compromise.

jobs.title: Supporter Led Fundraising Officer
jobs.description:
Your mission

Reporting to the Supporter Led Fundraising Manager, you'll support and inspire people to fundraise for CALM in their own way, providing the tools, encouragement and support they need to make an impact and build a meaningful relationship with CALM.

Responsibilities
Supporter engagement & stewardship

  • Provide excellent stewardship to CALM's Supporter Led fundraisers, acting as a fundraising coach to help people bring their ideas to life and make the most of their fundraising.
  • Build and develop relationships with supporters across DIY, challenges, in memory, tribute and other Supporter Led fundraising, providing personalised and compassionate support throughout their journey with CALM.
  • Ensure in memory and tribute supporters receive sensitive and appropriate stewardship, recognising the individual needs of people fundraising following a bereavement.
  • Support with the development and delivery of supporter journeys, communications and fundraising materials, including through Marketing Cloud, to deepen engagement and build longer-term supporter relationships.
  • Represent CALM at Supporter Led fundraising activities and events, helping to provide a brilliant experience for our supporters.

Fundraising growth & development
  • Contribute to CALM's fundraising targets through excellent relationship management, identifying opportunities to grow income and deepen supporter relationships.

Collaborative working

  • Build strong relationships across CALM, working collaboratively to create joined up experiences and make the most of opportunities for our supporters.

Your profile

Essential

Why us?

Reports to: Supporter Led Fundraising Manager

jobs.description:
Your mission

CALM’s digital products play an important role in helping people find support when they need it. Your job is to make that experience even better.

You’ll be at the heart of a collaborative team, leading the development and continuous improvement of the CALMzone app. You’ll turn user insight, data and ideas into intuitive, accessible experiences. You’ll work across product, design, research, data and technology, with plenty of scope to shape the app and contribute to CALM’s wider digital ecosystem.

Your profile

Product Strategy & Delivery

  • Deliver the mobile product strategy, as defined by the Senior Product Manager.
  • Manage the app through all stages of the lifecycle: discovery through to optimisation and iteration.
  • Own the continuous improvement of the app, including accessibility, onboarding and bootflow.
  • Manage the app’s technical health and stability across a range of devices.
  • Create, maintain, and prioritise product backlogs, ensuring alignment with organisation goals and user needs.
  • Define user stories with acceptance criteria and guide development teams through delivery.

  • Act as a UX lead mapping and optimising mobile user journeys, ensuring they are intuitive, inclusive, and insight-led.

  • Champion user-centred design and accessibility best practices.
  • Collaborate with mobile researchers, UI/UX designers, app developers, and agencies to ensure excellent delivery.

  • Engage with stakeholders at all levels to gather requirements, align priorities, and report progress.
  • Act as a translator between technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Promote a data-driven, test-and-learn culture across teams.
  • Ensure that the CALMzone app is strategically aligned.
  • Continuous Improvement
  • Monitor and analyse app performance using data, analytics, and feedback loops.
  • Drive a culture of continuous optimisation and regular update cadence.
  • Keep up-to-date with product management best practices, trends, OS and app store trends, bringing innovations into the CALMzone app.

Your profile 
Competencies
  • Mobile app lifecycle management
  • Product strategy
  • Agile execution and delivery
  • Data-driven decision making
  • Stakeholder management
  • Cross-functional collaboration - working with both technical and non-technical teams

Experience
  • Hands-on Mobile app experience: 2+ years of experience as a Product Manager launching and/or running a mobile app. Junior or associate Product Managers will be considered.
  • Experience managing an app through the full product lifecycle, including familiarity with App Store and Google Play releases processes.
  • Strong UX background with experience leading user journey mapping, defining user stories, and ensuring inclusive, accessible design.
  • Excellent ability to work across teams and with external partners (designers, developers, agencies).
  • Strong analytical skills, using data and research to inform decisions.
  • Confident communicator and stakeholder manager, able to champion product thinking across CALM.

Desirable Skills & Experience 
  • Experience managing web platforms, CMS development, or digital products alongside mobile apps.
  • Experience with livechat products such as WhatsApp, or AWS webchat.
  • Familiarity with CRM systems (especially Salesforce) and integration with mobile app data.
  • Experience working in an environment where time-management, prioritisation and adaptability are key.
  • Awareness of the not-for-profit or charity sector, or experience working with diverse user groups.


Why us?

  • Reports to: Senior Product Manager
  • Contract: Full-time, permanent
  • Benefits: Unlimited annual leave, Healthcare cash plan, 6% pension contribution, therapeutic services (after completion of probation), hybrid working & nine day fortnight
  • Based: London Waterloo twice a week (Wednesdays and Thursdays) / Remote Working (Mon, Tues & Fri), 9.30am - 5.30pm.
  • Salary: £38,000 - £45,000. We benchmark our salaries to ensure our pay structure remains fair, transparent, and equitable for everyone in our team.

A work environment that values creativity, personal growth and collaboration.

jobs.title: Supply Chain Controller (all genders)
jobs.description:
Willkommen bei Glow25!

Bei Glow25 verbinden wir Beauty mit Wissenschaft und modernster Technologie – KI gehört bei uns ganz selbstverständlich zum Arbeitsalltag. Als Deutschlands führende Kollagen-Marke begleiten wir Menschen dabei, sich in jeder Lebensphase wohlzufühlen und ihre natürliche Schönheit zu unterstreichen.

Für unser weiteres Wachstum suchen wir Menschen mit Substanz: zuverlässig, motiviert und mit echtem Interesse daran, gemeinsam etwas Bedeutendes aufzubauen. Bei Glow25 triffst du auf ambitionierte Ziele und ein Umfeld, das Eigenverantwortung fördert und Leistung wertschätzt – unabhängig davon, welche Rolle du übernimmst.

Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.

Das sind unsere aktuellen Herausforderungen und perspektivischen Ziele:

Als Supply Chain Controller (all genders) baust du ein modernes Controlling für unsere Lieferkette auf und agierst als Business Partner für unser Operations Management Team. Du sorgst für Transparenz in einem Bereich, der für unser Wachstum entscheidend ist, und bringst deine Controlling-Expertise direkt in operative Entscheidungen ein.

In diesem Bereich brauchen wir Deine Unterstützung:

  • Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für die Vorratsbewertung und entwickelst das Inventory Controlling kontinuierlich weiter.

  • Du baust Transparenz über Bestände, Warenbewegungen und deren finanziellen Einfluss auf.

  • Du analysierst zentrale Supply-Chain- und Operations-KPIs wie Bestände, COGS, Logistikkosten und Forecast Accuracy.

  • Du agierst als Business Partner für Operations, Supply Chain und Procurement und bringst finanzielle Perspektiven in operative Entscheidungen ein.

  • Du unterstützt bei Budgetplanung, Forecasts und der operativen Finanzplanung.

  • Du baust Dashboards, Reportingstrukturen und KPIs auf und entwickelst sie weiter.

  • Du erstellst Business Cases für operative Entscheidungen, zum Beispiel zu Lieferanten, Logistikstrukturen oder Bestandsstrategien.

  • Du identifizierst Kosten- und Working-Capital-Optimierungspotenziale entlang der gesamten Wertschöpfungskette.

Du bringst folgende Erfahrungen mit:

  • Du hast ein Studium der Betriebswirtschaft, Finance, Supply Chain Management, Wirtschaftswissenschaften oder eines vergleichbaren Fachbereichs abgeschlossen.

  • Du bringst mehrjährige Berufserfahrung im Controlling, Operations Finance, Supply Chain Analytics oder Consulting mit.

  • Du hast einschlägige Erfahrungen mit Beständen, Kostenstrukturen oder operativen KPIs.

  • Du denkst analytisch, arbeitest datengetrieben und kannst komplexe Zusammenhänge klar und verständlich aufbereiten.

  • Du arbeitest strukturiert und eigenständig und behältst auch in einem dynamischen Umfeld den Überblick.

  • Du hast sehr gute Kenntnisse in Excel oder Google Sheets und bewegst dich sicher in der Welt der Zahlen.

  • Du hast Erfahrung mit BI-Tools wie Power BI oder Tableau oder bist motiviert, dich schnell einzuarbeiten.

  • Du hast idealerweise bereits mit ERP-Systemen oder Finanzsystemen gearbeitet.

  • Du interessierst dich für Datenanalyse, Reporting und die Entwicklung aussagekräftiger KPIs.

Das sind Charakterzüge, die Dich beschreiben:

• Du bist analytisch stark und liebst es, komplexe Zusammenhänge zu durchdringen.
• Du bist ein Teamplayer mit ausgeprägter Kommunikationsstärke.
• Du arbeitest strukturiert, eigenverantwortlich und lösungsorientiert.
• Du bist proaktiv und bringst Themen selbstständig voran.
• Du bist flexibel und behältst auch in dynamischen Situationen den Überblick.

Diese Rolle passt eher nicht zu dir, wenn...

  • ...du am liebsten für dich allein arbeitest und wenig Austausch mit anderen Teams suchst. Die Rolle lebt vom laufenden Business Partnering mit Production, Supply Chain und Procurement.

  • ...dir der Einstieg ins Controlling noch fehlt. Wir suchen jemanden mit bereits gefestigter Praxiserfahrung, nicht für eine Einstiegsposition.

  • ...du dich ungern mit Tabellen, Kennzahlen und Datenanalyse beschäftigst. Excel/Google Sheets sind hier tägliches Handwerkszeug.

  • ...du feste Prozesse ohne Weiterentwicklung bevorzugst.

Darauf kannst du dich freuen:

  • Arbeite flexibel, so wie es am besten zu dir passt. Arbeite dann und dort, wo du am produktivsten bist – mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten und smarter Zeiterfassung.

  • Glow Card – jeden Monat ein Bonus. 50 € Guthaben monatlich für lokale Anbieter – macht 600 € im Jahr extra für dich.

  • Weiterkommen leicht gemacht. Mit unserer Glowcademy und Lernzeit pro Woche bleibst du immer am Ball.

  • 40 % Mitarbeiterrabatt. Auf das komplette Sortiment – das lohnt sich wirklich.

  • Urlaub, der dir guttut. 30 Tage frei + 1 persönlicher Feiertag + bis zu 10 unbezahlte Tage extra, wenn du mal länger abschalten willst.

  • Gesundheit im Fokus. Wir übernehmen bis zu 600 € im Jahr für Zusatzleistungen – von Brille bis Zahnreinigung.

  • Für später gut abgesichert. Nach der Probezeit gibt’s 600 € Zuschuss zur Altersvorsorge – und wenn du selbst mit einzahlst, legen wir nochmal 20 % drauf.

  • Corporate Benefits & FutureBens. Hol dir exklusive Rabatte und Vorteile bei vielen Partnern.

  • Kultur, die wirklich strahlt. Seit fünf Jahren in Folge sind wir als Top Company bei Kununu ausgezeichnet - ein echtes Zeichen für unsere starke, positive und gelebte Kultur.

  • Move your way. Vom Workout bis zur Wellness-Auszeit - du entscheidest, wie du dich fit hältst. Mit Urban Sports Club oder Wellpass hast du die Wahl.

Yay! Du hast es bis hierher geschafft!

Wenn du jetzt immer noch liest, ist die Wahrscheinlichkeit groß, dass wir ein Match sind.

Eine Sache liegt uns aber noch am Herzen: Trau dich! Vor allem als Frau oder als jemand einer unterrepräsentierten Bevölkerungsgruppe. Auch wenn du nicht überall einen Haken setzen kannst, möchten wir dich ermutigen, dich trotzdem zu bewerben. Wir glauben, dass eine bunte Vielfalt von Perspektiven und Erfahrungen ein Team stärker macht – und je stärker unser Team ist, desto besser erreichen wir unsere Mission, Menschen zu mehr Energie im Alltag zu verhelfen.

jobs.title: Future Sales Community @SoSafe – Talent Pool für SDRs (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Bist du bereit, deine Sales-Karriere in einer der aktuell spannendsten, wachsendsten und beständigsten Branchen zu starten oder auf das nächste Level zu bringen?

Wenn du bereits im Vertrieb reingeschnuppert hast und in einem der dynamischsten und innovativsten Unternehmen weiter wachsen möchtest, dann ist SoSafe dein Next Step!

Wir bei SoSafe haben das Ziel, der führende Anbieter für Human Risk Management Lösungen in Europa zu werden. Unsere preisgekrönte Awareness-Plattform unterstützt Unternehmen dabei, nachhaltige Verhaltensänderungen durch effektive, interaktive Trainings rund um Cyber-Sicherheit und Datenschutz zu erzielen. Cyberkriminalität kostet die Welt jährlich >$10 Billionen, mit steigenden Kosten um 15 % pro Jahr – werde Teil der Lösung und gestalte die Zukunft der Cybersicherheit aktiv mit!

Wie funktioniert’s?

Bewirb dich einmal und werde Teil unseres Talent Pools. Unser Sales Development Team entwickelt sich kontinuierlich, doch nicht immer stimmt das Timing für eine Bewerbung. Mit dem Talentpool stellen wir sicher, dass wir keine Talente verpassen und bieten dir gleichzeitig die Möglichkeit, dein Interesse zu bekunden.

Sobald sich eine passende Stelle abzeichnet, melden wir uns proaktiv bei dir, um ein Erstgespräch zu vereinbaren – oft schon vor der offiziellen Ausschreibung. So kommen wir auf dich zu und drehen den Spieß um!

In der Zwischenzeit bleibst du mit uns in Kontakt und erhältst spannende Einblicke in das Unternehmen.

Das ist deine Chance, wirklich etwas zu bewegen und deine Karriere im Sales zu starten.
Wenn du motiviert, neugierig und bereit bist, deine Zukunft im Tech Sales aufzubauen, freuen wir uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen!

So trägst du zum Erfolg bei:

  • Du sprichst gezielt B2B-Kunden an – per Cold Calling, E-Mail, LinkedIn und weiteren Outbound-Taktiken.

  • Du hast täglich Cold Calling Blöcke und planst strukturierte Outreach-Aktivitäten – in dieser Rolle ist täglicher Outbound ein Muss.

  • Du qualifizierst eingehende Leads und identifizierst Accounts mit hohem Potenzial für weitere Gespräche.

  • Du vereinbarst Meetings mit Kunden und entwickelst frühe Opportunities weiter, um unsere Sales-Pipeline zu füllen.

  • Du hältst alle Interaktionen, Notizen und Opportunity-Status aktuell und sauber im CRM fest.

  • Du arbeitest auf ambitionierte Ziele hin und gibst jeden Tag 100%, um sie zu erreichen oder zu übertreffen.

  • Du baust ein tiefes Verständnis für unser Produkt, unsere Buyer Personas und die Wettbewerbslandschaft auf.

  • Du nutzt modernste Tools und Prozesse wie Automatisierungs-Workflows, KI-Systeme und arbeitest mit RevOps- und Go-To-Market-Engineering- Teams, um einen erstklassigen Pipeline Generierungsprozess zu gewährleisten.

Was dich auszeichnet:

  • Erste Erfahrung in einer kundenorientierten Rolle (z.B. Sales Development, Promotion, Door-to-door Vertrieb, Kundenservice oder Recruiting) ist ein Plus.

  • Du bist lernwillig und offen für konstruktives Feedback.

  • Du kommunizierst klar, hörst aktiv zu und trittst im Kundendialog selbstbewusst auf.

  • Du bleibst auch unter Druck organisiert und verfolgst deine Ziele fokussiert.

  • Du fühlst dich wohl in einem schnelllebigen, dynamischen Umfeld mit schnellen Entscheidungswegen und wenig starren Prozessen.

  • Du bringst ein Growth Mindset mit und gibst nicht auf, wenn’s mal herausfordernd wird – du willst dich weiterentwickeln!

  • Du bist performance-orientiert und möchtest mit deinen Ergebnissen überzeugen.

  • Erfahrung mit CRM- und Outreach-Tools ist ein Plus.

  • Du bist bereit, mindestens 3 Tage pro Woche in unserem Büro in Köln oder Berlin zu arbeiten (hybrides Modell).

  • Du sprichst Deutsch fließend und hast gute Sprachkenntnisse in Englisch.

Was wir bieten*:

  • Work-Life-Balance: Flexible Arbeitszeiten, 33 Tage Urlaub

  • Well-being und finanzielle Unterstützung: Zugang zur Open-Up App, Mitarbeiterrabatte

  • Verbindung & Gemeinschaft: Virtuelle Events, gemeinsame Teamaktivitäten und Möglichkeiten für lokale Treffen

  • Und vieles mehr: Technische Ausstattung, Empfehlungsprämien, hundefreundliches Büro

*Die oben genannten Vergünstigungen gelten für Vollzeitmitarbeiter und können je nach Standort leicht variieren. Dies ist nur eine Auswahl – mehr erfahren Sie im Verlauf des Bewerbungsprozesses.

Über uns

Wir bei SoSafe haben es uns zur Aufgabe gemacht, die digitale Welt sicherer zu gestalten, indem wir den menschlichen Faktor in der Cybersicherheit in den Mittelpunkt stellen.
Als eines der am schnellsten wachsenden Security-Awareness-Scale-ups weltweit nutzen wir verhaltenswissenschaftliche Erkenntnisse und datengesteuertes Lernen, um Menschen effektiv gegen Cyber-Bedrohungen zu stärken. Unser Human Risk Management-Ansatz unterstützt Unternehmen dabei, ihre Mitarbeiter*innen zum wirkungsvollsten Schutzschild gegen Sicherheitsrisiken zu entwickeln.

Mit der Unterstützung führender VCs wie Highland Europe und Global Founders Capital expandieren wir weltweit in rasantem Tempo. Wir suchen Teamplayer, die sinnvolle Veränderungen im Bereich Cybersicherheit vorantreiben, Verantwortung übernehmen und gemeinsam mit uns wachsen wollen.

Wenn du in einem lebendigen, zielorientierten Umfeld aufblühst, das Innovation, Vielfalt und Zusammenarbeit groß schreibt – dann bist du bei uns genau richtig!

jobs.title: Junior Automation Engineer - Facilities SCADA & PLC (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
The Role

We are looking for a Junior Automation Engineer to grow into the technical care of the Facilities Monitoring and Control System (FMCS) behind our fab - the system that supervises every utility our production depends on, from cleanroom air and chilled water to process cooling, exhaust and power monitoring. Here's the best part: you'll join during the final commissioning phase, working side by side with the specialists who bring the system to life. You'll learn it hands-on while the people who built it are still on site - and grow, step by step, into independent ownership. It's about as good a launchpad for a career in automation engineering as you'll find.

To join our team, you should be excited to:

  • Support the operation, monitoring and maintenance of our SCADA system (Siemens WinCC OA) and our Siemens S7-1500 PLCs

  • Take part in loop checks - learning to trace each signal from the field device through I/O and PLC to the operator screen, and to confirm that commands move valves, dampers and actuators; one of the fastest ways to understand the whole system

  • Help investigate and resolve alarms and faults during commissioning and live operation

  • Support instrument calibration checks and field-signal troubleshooting

  • Help build datapoints, screens, trends and reports, and keep documentation up to date

  • Gradually take on more system responsibility as your confidence grows

  • Work closely with experienced colleagues and with our facility and IT teams

Your Qualifications

  • One of two equivalent qualification paths: a completed apprenticeship as an Electronics Technician for Automation Technology plus further training as a state-certified technician (Techniker), or comparable - or a degree in Electrical Engineering, Automation Engineering or a related field, or comparable

  • 2–3 years of professional experience with initial hands-on exposure

  • Basic knowledge of PLC programming and/or SCADA - ideally in a Siemens environment (S7 / TIA Portal, WinCC OA), but a solid foundation on comparable platforms plus a willingness to learn ours is just as welcome

  • Curiosity about how a large automation system fits together - from field instrument to operator screen - and eagerness to learn loop checks, diagnostics and commissioning on the real system

  • A careful, team-oriented way of working

  • Good command of English; German is an advantage

jobs.description:

The system is delivered and commissioned by an external integrator; from handover, it's yours. You won't be building it from scratch - you'll be the person who understands it well enough to keep it running, diagnose it when it misbehaves, extend it as we grow from pilot line to full production, and hold suppliers to account.   • Operate, monitor and maintain our SCADA system (Siemens WinCC OA) across servers, operator stations and displays

  • Maintain and diagnose our Siemens S7-1500 PLCs and their remote I/O, and adapt control logic within the existing standardised structure

  • Plan and perform loop checks end to end - tracing each signal from the field device through wiring, I/O and PLC all the way to the operator screen, and confirming that commands actually move valves, dampers and actuators

  • Investigate and resolve alarms, communication faults and unexpected equipment behaviourduring live operation

  • Verify instrument calibration and troubleshoot analog and digital field signals - multimeter in hand, not only from a screen

  • Add new datapoints, screens, trends and reports, and tune alarms so operators trust the system

  • Keep documentation current - as-built drawings, tag lists, change records - and uphold change control

  • Act as the technical counterpart to contractors and vendors, and support qualification and audits with system evidence

jobs.description:
Your Role & How we work

As our Engineer - Data & Platforms (m/f/d), you build and run the internal data products that our investment team, Quantitative Research and AI Engineering rely on every day: the pipelines, datasets, APIs and tools that turn a large and growing pool of financial and alternative data into something investors can act on. Our stack is Python, SQL, AWS, and Databricks.

You report to Anton Popov, Director of Engineering. This is a hands-on engineering role: most of your time goes to designing, building, and shipping. The team is small, so you take ownership of real products early, and you get a manager and colleagues invested in your growth into investment and data-platform topics. You work closely with Quantitative Research, AI Engineering, Product & Data, and the investment team, and we treat agentic AI as a default in how we build.

What you will do

  • Build and improve the internal products the investment and research teams use daily: data pipelines, datasets, APIs, and tooling, on top of our lakehouse and orchestration stack.

  • Work directly with the teams you build for: take in their requests, triage and prioritise them, protect the integrity and consistency of the product, and explain features and implementation trade-offs in clear, non-technical language.

  • Design, build, and operate reliable data pipelines, ETLs and integrations that handle complex financial and alternative datasets.

  • Bring and reinforce good engineering habits in the team: automated testing at several levels, CI/CD, pull requests and code review, and clear documentation.

  • Contribute to operational excellence: observability, monitoring, data quality, and secure data handling.

  • Use agentic AI across engineering work (coding, review, testing, debugging, documentation) and help the team push these practices forward.


The experience you bring

  • 3 to 5 years of professional software or data engineering experience, building and operating systems in production.

  • Strong Python and strong SQL, with clean, readable code and a good sense for data modelling.

  • Proven engineering discipline: you write tests (unit, integration, data quality), work with CI/CD, and use pull requests and code review as a matter of course, and you can show how you helped a team adopt them.

  • Clear communication with non-engineers: you can explain what you built, why, and what it will and will not do, and you can say no constructively.

  • Hands-on use of AI across engineering functions, including frontier coding systems such as Claude Code and Codex, as a core part of how you work.

  • Genuine interest in investing, financial markets and data, and the ambition to grow into these topics.

  • Nice to have: Databricks or PySpark; data platform tooling such as orchestration (Airflow, Dagster or similar), lakehouse formats (Parquet, Delta, Iceberg) and AWS; experience with investment, financial or market data; building web frontends or APIs for internal tools; LLM systems in production.


2 reasons why you should not apply

  • You prefer fully specified tickets and no contact with users. Here the people you build for sit next to you, ask for things directly, and expect you to weigh in on what should be built and how.

  • You treat AI tooling as an occasional helper. We expect agentic AI to be a default in how you build, review, test, and ship, every day, not now and then.


Your mindset

  • You are a builder who loves to ship: pragmatic on trade-offs, careful on quality. You move fast, but fast does not mean sloppy.

  • You care about correctness, reliability, security, and long-term maintainability, and you leave codebases and teams better than you found them.

  • You are curious about how investment decisions are made and want to understand the data behind them, not just move it.

  • You see AI-powered development as a competitive advantage, not a novelty, and use agentic AI as a core part of how you work.

  • You communicate clearly on progress, trade-offs, and risk, and you own problems end-to-end.


What we offer

  • Work with petabytes of data and the most cutting-edge tools in and beyond asset management, with Day 1 ownership of challenging, varied work and a steep learning curve.

  • Become part of a unique success story in European asset management, alongside the most knowledgeable experts in the industry on one of the most consequential investment themes of the next decade.

  • A motivated, highly international team (15 nationalities) that gathers in person at our Berlin HQ and supports each other, with flat hierarchies and direct interaction with our management team and investors.

  • Visa sponsorship, relocation support, and a competitive compensation package with a meaningful variable component tied to fund performance.

jobs.title: Full Stack Software Engineer (Angular/Python)
jobs.description:
Position Overview:

This is a vacancy for a hybrid role with regular visits to our HQ in Tutzing, Germany or Amsterdam, the Netherlands. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender identity. 

We are building out the cloud services around the Lobster Data Platform, and we are looking for a Full Stack Software Engineer to join us. What you would build sits between the platform and the people who run it: dashboards that show what is actually happening in a customer's integrations, control planes for provisioning and configuration, self-service tooling that takes routine work off our operations team, and the monitoring around all of it. Python and its API on the backend, Angular on the front end, and you would work on both sides. 

What our customers see is the software you create, so we care as much about how you think about our users as about how you code. The best ideas here tend to come from engineers who ask what someone is trying to achieve and then make that easier. You will have the freedom to bring those ideas to Product Management and to build them. 

Ready to make an impact? 


You’ll get to take ownership of:

  • Developing our Python backend as a product: data model, business logic, validation, migrations, automated tests.
  • Designing and maintaining the RESTful API on top of it, so that services, front-ends and neighbouring systems communicate cleanly.
  • Defining and implementing scalable microservices, from the schema through to deployment.
  • Building the Angular front-end that sits on that API, together with a colleague from the team: components, state, routing and the tests that go with them.
  • Operating and maintaining what you build: containerized, stateless services on AWS, deployed through CI/CD rather than by hand, with monitoring and alerting that tells you something before a customer does.
  • Keeping the running system healthy over time, from dependency and version upgrades to cost and configuration.
  • Evaluating and selecting the tools and technologies that fit a given engineering problem
  • Working closely with Product Management on what the software should do: bringing your own ideas about what customers need, where their work is still harder than it has to be, and how a step could be made simpler.
  • Improving the practices around all of this, from pipelines to test coverage to how we handle incidents.
None of the following is a hard requirement. The more of it you bring, the sooner you can take on that part of the role, and the rest you can pick up here: 
  • A DevOps mindset in practice: you have looked after services you wrote, not handed them over the wall.
  • AWS experience beyond a certification: compute, networking, storage and identity, and a sense of what a design decision costs.
  • Serverless patterns alongside long-running services, and a view on when each one is the right choice.
  • Infrastructure as Code with Terraform or CloudFormation.
  • CI/CD with GitHub Actions or something comparable.
  • Monitoring, logging and alerting: you have set these up rather than only read the dashboards.


We’d love to meet someone with:

  • Around three to five years of professional software engineering with Python as your primary language, and experience running what you built in production.
  • Python craft: strictly typed, well-structured application code. You have built and maintained a backend and its API, not scripts and notebooks, and you model your data at every boundary with Pydantic or something similar.
  • Experience with a web framework such as FastAPI, and with relational databases: schema design, an ORM like SQLAlchemy, and migrations you can run without holding your breath
  • Practical async Python: you have built services on asyncio and you know why a single blocking call inside a coroutine stalls everything around it.
  • Angular and TypeScript on the front end. You can build new components where the product needs them, not only adjust what is already there.
  • A production mindset (you build it, you run it). You think about pipelines, maintainability, testing, telemetry and debugging, and you are willing to be part of working out why something broke
  • A feel for what goes wrong across a network boundary: timeouts, bounded retries with backoff, idempotency.
  • Working knowledge of Docker and of building services that hold no state of their own
  • An eye for the people on the other side of the screen. You ask what a customer is actually trying to get done, and you would rather remove a step than document it.
  • A creative, independent way of working. You are given a goal and room to find the route, and you enjoy filling in the parts that nobody has specified yet.
  • A natural instinct for security. Our software handles customer data and customer environments, so you think about access, secrets and validation while you write, not afterwards.
  • Strong communication skills in English. German is desirable, but not a requirement.


You can look forward to:

  • Opportunity to work flexibly from home 
  • Modern offices in Germany and the Netherlands
  • A personal Learning & Development budget 
  • Up to 30 days of remote work per year from any EU country 
  • Company Pension plan 
  • 30 vacation days a year 
  • 2 additional paid days off on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve
  • Location-specific benefits packages (your recruiter will be happy to provide more details during your first chat) 
  • Company-sponsored business travel

For this role, we are open to working with specialists based in Germany or the Netherlands. Whether you prefer working on-site at our offices in Tutzing, Amsterdam, or remotely from a location within one of these countries, we’re happy to accommodate your preferred working style. 
 
If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply!  
 
Lobster is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive environment where empathy and respect guide our interactions.
